This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Vnukovo International Airport in degrees Celsius on 1 May '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column on the specified date once information is finalized for all hours on that date, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=UUWW

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve to "Yes" until data for this date has been finalized.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Any revisions to temperatures recorded after data is finalized for this market's timeframe will not be considered for this market's resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects a prolonged cold anomaly gripping Moscow, with official forecasts from Roshydromet and Yandex Weather projecting May 1 highs of 7–9°C amid persistent northerly airflow channeling Arctic air masses southward. Recent observations show April 28–29 maxima near 3–6°C under cloudy, drizzly conditions, well below the 16°C climatological average for early May, due to a blocking high-pressure system stalling warm advection. The tight race between 8°C (34%) and 9°C (28%) stems from model divergences—ECMWF ensembles slightly warmer at ~11°C versus local GFS runs cooler—plus uncertainty in diurnal cloud cover suppressing peaks. Watch for tomorrow's 12Z model runs, as timing of any clearing could tip the balance by 1–2°C.

Over the past 24-48 hours, updated model runs have trended cooler, with ensemble means clustering in the upper 60s to low 70s amid 30-50% precipitation chances. New 12z NWS discussions and overnight model cycles could shift odds if the front accelerates eastward.
